Evaluation · ruled 2026-10-18: E1–E6 all as recommended

Chat pauses now; messaging comes back for families, in a different shape

Chat as built is the least valuable slice of messaging (staff only), delivered unreliably (phone notifications only: an iPhone needs the app installed, Android delivery has never been confirmed, and nothing is emailed), beside email tools that already reach the same people. Its real prize, families, was cut on 2026-08-01 for safety reasons that mostly still hold. Pausing is cheap and reversible: chat is not sold on any plan card, not in the demos, and no paying customer uses it. When messaging returns it should be announcements that reach everyone, with replies, on rosters the product already knows.

Why it feels unused, in order of weight

  1. Nobody can rely on it. A rain delay reaches only coaches who installed the app, allowed notifications, and have a device where delivery works.
  2. A small audience behind a tab everyone sees. Fans, families, club staff and house-league coaches can never use it.
  3. It duplicates the email tools, and the email one reaches everyone.
  4. Staff-only chat is where WhatsApp is strongest. The audiences where a platform wins (families, a whole club's coaches, every coach at an event) are the ones chat never had or covered unreliably.
If messaging returns: two screens, to judge E2 and E4

Chat — keep it, change it, or pause it? (evaluation, 2026-10-18)

Owner, 2026-10-18, after the Chat Consistency walk: "users in an organization have no chat. I am considering removing chat entirely from the app for the time being if we can't get this right … it is a very seldom used feature, many people are already stuck using the chat apps they are familiar with … can you do a deep evaluation of a holistic unified chat experience, taking into consideration eventually including family members of house league and rep players … does it make sense to have separate chats or a unified one? does it make sense to have chats at all … are there users or portals that do not need or should not have chats vs ones that should?"

Lives on the Chat hub's Evaluation tab (https://claude.ai/artifact/HsTsarRgc4fxjtLZ8Z3DVQ). The Chat Consistency plan (CHAT_CONSISTENCY_PLAN.md) is the answer to a narrower question; E1 shelves it.

⚖ RULED 2026-10-18 (owner, pasted from the hub): E1–E6 all as recommended. Chat pauses now: every door hidden, the rooms and messages kept. Messaging returns as announcements-with-replies that reach everyone (E2), for families in the Club tier on the safeguarding rules (E3), through one inbox with portals as doors (E4), for the audiences in §7 (E5); the email tools stay as they are meanwhile (E6). Next: the /strategy entry (it supersedes the permanent Chat tab of 2026-07-18 and 2026-07-20 and the free portal's Chat door of 2026-10-15), then the pause's build prompt.

The short answer

Pause chat now. Bring messaging back later in a different shape, for families, when the Club tier is ready for them.

Chat as built is the least valuable slice of messaging, delivered unreliably, beside email tools that already do the same jobs and reach everyone. Its real prize (families, the part every competitor builds around) was cut on 2026-08-01 for safety reasons that still mostly hold. Making today's chat consistent (the four-stage ladder) would not change any of that. Pausing is cheap and reversible: chat is not sold on any plan card, not in the demos, and no paying customer uses it (the product is pre-revenue). When messaging returns, it should be announcements that reach everyone, with replies, built on the rosters the product already knows: "Messages", not "Chat".

1 · What chat is today

Who has it. Two room kinds exist: an event's All coaches room and its division rooms (tournament organizers on Tournament Plus and up, and the coaches of registered teams who have signed in), and a rep team's staff room (head coach and assistants on the Premium Coaches Portal or a Club plan).

RoleChat today
Tournament organizer (owner, admin, staff with the tournaments module)Yes, in Plus events: moderates All coaches and division rooms
Coach in a tournament (paid or free portal)Yes, once signed in and linked to a registered team
Rep team head coach and assistants (Premium, Club)Yes: the staff room
Club admins, registrars, treasurersNo. The club admin has no chat section (owners, admins and staff get a seat only in their own events' rooms)
House-league coaches and volunteersNo. They have no accounts (a free-text name on the team)
Families and guardiansNo. Family chat was cut 2026-08-01; the guardian tier is built but switched off pending counsel
Fans and followersNo, but they see a Chat tab with a sample conversation and a pitch

Where it lives. The home app's bottom bar (a permanent Chat tab, for everyone), both coaches portals, and the tournament admin. Not the club admin.

How a message reaches someone who is not looking at the app. Only by phone notification. On an iPhone that needs the app added to the home screen first. Android delivery in production has never been confirmed (a suspected key mismatch is on record). Chat sends no email and writes no bell entry. No chat screen asks for notification permission.

What else already talks to the same people, reliably, by email:

  • the tournament admin's Communications (Messages on the phone bar): an announcement emailed to every team's contact, posted on the public site, pushed to fans who follow (it already replaces Chat on events without it);
  • the coaches portal's Email families (one-way, to the guardian emails on the roster);
  • the club's message a household, the house-league season email, and Ask the coaches.

2 · Why it feels unused (four reasons, in order of weight)

1. Nobody can rely on it. A rain delay posted in chat reaches the coaches who installed the app and allowed notifications on a device where delivery works. Everyone else finds out late or never. An organizer learns this once and goes back to email or a WhatsApp group. No layout fixes this. 2. Its audience is small, behind a tab everyone sees. Only organizers of Plus events, coaches who signed up, and paid rep staff can use it. Fans, families, club staff and house-league coaches (most people who open the home app) meet a Chat tab that will never hold anything for them. 3. It duplicates the email tools. An organizer has two places to tell coaches something, and the email one reaches everyone. The coach has a staff room and Email families. Two tools for one job means the familiar one wins. 4. Staff-only chat is where WhatsApp is strongest. Coaches already have a staff group and know each other's numbers. The platform adds little there. The audiences where a platform beats WhatsApp (families, a club's whole coaching staff, every coach at an event) are the ones chat either never had or covered unreliably.

3 · What the market does, and what the rules require

  • Competitors converge on two things: an automatic team room that includes parents, and a one-way announcement with a seen count, delivered by email or text to anyone without the app (GameChanger, Heja, TeamSnap, SportsEngine, LeagueApps, PlayMetrics). Staff-only chat is a side feature everywhere.
  • Safeguarding rules in Canada do not ban team chat; they ban private contact with minors. The Coaching Association of Canada's electronic-communication guidelines and Rule of Two: no one-on-one texting or online contact between a coach and an athlete; group messages include at least two adults; parents of minor athletes can receive them; communication should be recorded and available to the organization. The Universal Code of Conduct (2025) lists "communicating privately with a Minor through social media or text" as a boundary transgression (a minor is under 19). Softball Canada's policy: team communication on WhatsApp should include parents.
  • The guidelines also say families must not be required to use a platform to get team information. So in-app messaging can never be the only channel; announcements must also go by email.
  • Products that include minors build the controls in: Spond's messaging age limit and guardian tab; Heja's default parent monitoring; LeagueApps' under-18 chat permission and admin deletion.

4 · Where a platform genuinely beats WhatsApp

1. The audience builds itself from registrations and rosters: nobody collects phone numbers, and people join and leave as teams change. 2. It reaches across clubs: an organizer cannot easily build a WhatsApp group of 40 visiting coaches; the event already knows them. 3. It protects minors: no personal numbers shared, at least two adults, parents included, a record the club can see, no private adult–minor messages. 4. The sender sees who read it: "seen by 18 of 22 coaches" tells an organizer whom to phone. 5. It is tied to the season: a schedule change or a cancelled practice can post itself.

All five are strongest in announcements with replies to families and to large coach groups. Today's chat delivers one of them (2) unreliably and the others not at all.

5 · The options

Pause now (recommended)Keep and fixKeep as is
What people seeNo Chat tab or chat item anywhere; the home bar becomes Home · Scores · Account; organizers use Messages (Communications), as on events without chat todayOne consistent chat on four doors, a reach fix (confirmed Android delivery, a push prompt, organizer posts also emailed), the Chat tab only for people with roomsToday's four versions
What it costsOne bounded build: hide the doors, retire chat copy and help, keep the rooms and dataThe four-stage ladder plus the reach work: several sessions, all of it staff-onlyNothing now; every portal change keeps carrying chat
What we loseOrganizer↔coach rooms and staff rooms (no paying user); the Chat tab in the consumer bar (two 2026-07 rulings)Time that the Club launch needsTrust: the first real organizer finds half the coaches never saw the message
Families laterDesigned fresh on the framework belowBuilds on a staff-only shapeSame

Why pause rather than fix: fixing gets a consistent, staff-only chat that still depends on an app install to work. The valuable version is a different product (families, announcements, email reach, safeguarding), and the current one does not grow into it by polishing. Pausing returns attention to the Club launch and loses nothing a customer relies on.

What is not lost: the rooms, members and messages stay in the database; the engine (rooms built from rosters, moderators, reports, mute, remove, polls, receipts) is the base the framework reuses.

6 · The framework for when messaging returns

1. One inbox per person, every portal a door into it. Home holds everything you are part of; a portal opens the same inbox showing only what belongs there (a team's portal: that team; the tournament admin: that event; the club admin: the club), with a way out to everything. Never a separate chat system per portal. 2. Every room is an audience in a context, and its name says both: "Families · U13 Hawks", "All coaches · Spring Classic", "Coaches · Milton Minor Ball". The inbox groups rooms under their context with a small Event, Team or Club label, and each room's details say why you are in it ("you coach U13 Hawks"). 3. Two modes: an announcement (only staff or the organizer posts; everyone sees it; it reaches everyone by phone notification or email; the sender sees who has seen it) and a conversation (optional, for groups that want one, in-app). Most rooms start as announcements with replies. 4. Reach rules: an announcement always reaches every member: notification where it works, email everywhere else. Conversation messages never email individually (at most a daily summary). The app asks for notification permission the first time someone opens Messages. 5. Safeguarding rules, enforced by the system, not by the screen: no one-to-one messages between an adult and a player; players under 19 are not members (families are); any room with families has at least two adult staff; no family-to-family private messages; replies to an announcement go to the staff, not to every family; the club can see its teams' family rooms; messages are kept for the club's record; a report goes to the club, not to the coach. 6. What you can do follows who you are in the room, never the door you came in by. 7. Audiences come only from what the product already knows: a registration, a roster, a coaching role, a club membership. Nobody adds people by phone number, and there is no directory of strangers.

The measured walk · 2026-10-18

Four doors into one chat, and how far apart they are

Every surface draws its conversation with the same shared panel. They differ in the frame around it and, the walk found, in what a person may do inside it. Walked on the dev server at 390, 960 and 1280 wide, posting, replying, reacting, mentioning, searching and deleting on every surface, and posting from a second account while each list was open.

What the walk found first

  1. The organizer has no list, and the conversation gets 464 px on a phone against 557 to 646 elsewhere.
  2. What you can do depends on the door. The organizer opening a push lands at home, where they cannot moderate. Report and Mute exist only at home.
  3. No list updates while you look at it, on any surface; only the Chat tab's badge counts.
  4. Three list designs and two names for one room ("All coaches" and "UAT Chat Review Cup — Coaches").
  5. Press and hold means three things, and a tap floats buttons over the message above.
  6. A free-portal defect: opening any room with unread messages slides its header under the team banner.

1 · Arriving

As built

  • A Chat tab on every surface; its badge counts unread messages across every room you are in.
  • Every chat push (a message, an @mention) opens home chat at the room, for coaches and organizers alike. The coaches portal and the organizer's page never receive one.
  • A lone room opens by itself on home and both portals. The organizer always lands in All coaches.
  • A poll's push carries no room and opens the home page.

My read

The push is how most people arrive on game day, and it always lands at home. That is right for a coach. For an organizer it only fails because home will not let them moderate. Making home complete is cheaper and safer than sending each role somewhere else.

Shape questions
  • Keep pushes landing at home, with home made complete. Ask C4, beside drawing 9.

As built

Ruled 2026-10-18 (Ask 1, adopted with amendments)

The standard every door is measured against

Chat behaves like the messaging app people already know, on every surface. The owner's benchmark has pointed at WhatsApp since June: the June chat review ("fills the screen like iMessage and WhatsApp"), division rooms as a full-screen slide-over, Phase 3's "WhatsApp parity", the desktop split at full width, and an open room with no masthead (September).

RuleWhat it says
W1A phone opens on the list: the chats you can open, newest activity first, an unread count per row. A lone room may open straight into its conversation.
W2Tap a row and the conversation fills the screen: no title band, picker or banner above it. The app's bottom bar hides inside an open conversation (ruled 2026-10-18); back returns to the list, where it is.
W3The header is the only chrome: back on the left, the room's name over one line (who it reaches), search on the right. Back is always there on a phone and always goes to the list. Tapping the room's name opens its details: members, Mute, and Manage for whoever moderates.
W4The message box sits on the bottom edge, rides above the keyboard, and its hint says who the message reaches.
W5A computer is the split: the list left, the conversation right, the full width beside the portal's side menu, no back.
W6One behaviour per gesture: press and hold opens the same menu everywhere (its contents vary by role, never its place). Right-click opens that menu on a computer. Reply, react, mention, search, receipts, the unread line and pins work the same everywhere.
W7One breakpoint for list ↔ split on every surface. The walk sets it at 1024 (Ask D1 confirms).

Ask 0 · the 2026-10-18 organizer phone fix (§333)

Ruled: the phone layout undone (the hidden room header, the framed card, search in the pill row); the message box's hint naming who it reaches and the disabled Send's standard fade kept. The same screen's other fix (New room closes the rooms list and covers the phone bar, §332) was left alone.

Settled, not reopened

Staff rooms are per team and nobody inherits staff-room history (CH-5) · no chat email; push and the Chat tab's count only · family chat was cut · the free plan's Chat stays behind the Tournament Plus wall (A60) · a lone room opens by itself on home.

Standing back

The rules that cut across the stations

  • R1 · One chat, four doors. The same three parts on every door: the list, the open room, the room's details. A door decides which rooms are listed and the colours around them, nothing else.
  • R2 · What you can do follows who you are in the room, never the door. A moderator moderates on every door; a staff room's head coach pins on every door; everyone can reply, react, delete their own and mute everywhere, and everyone who does not moderate can report.
  • R3 · One list row, and a live list. Avatar, the room's one name, time, the last message with its sender, the unread count; Staff and Closed tags; a muted bell. A new message moves its row to the top and counts it.
  • R4 · One open room on a phone. It fills the screen. Header: ‹ · avatar · name over who it reaches · search. Nothing above, no bottom bar, the message box on the bottom edge at 16 px.
  • R5 · One message menu. Hold (phone), right-click or the hover ⌄ (computer): a row of reactions, then Reply · Copy · Pin (moderators) · Delete (yours) or Remove (moderators) · Report (someone else's, for anyone who does not moderate). A tap does nothing.
  • R6 · One room-details screen. Members, Mute, and for a moderator the coaches not yet joined, reports, Rename, Close and Delete. The organizer's Manage room becomes this screen.
  • R7 · One breakpoint, 1024.
The ladder

Four stages, each across all four doors

Each stage changes one part of the app on every door at once, so no stage leaves the surfaces further apart than it found them. The kickoff's draft built the organizer's phone first; built alone, that would have added a fourth list design before the shared row existed.

D One split, loose ends1024 everywhere; the organizer's split is list, room and a details panel; the portal's list column; a poll's push and the portal's sign-in both open the roomD1–D2Drawn 2026-10-18

Build order

A, then B, C and D. F08 can ship first, on its own: it is one scroll in the shared conversation, and free coaches meet it every time a room has unread messages.

What this does not change

No data, permission or notification change. C3 uses permissions the server already enforces; C4 keeps every push's link. The two link fixes in D make an existing link open the room it names.

Checks owed on a real phone

The iPhone zoom on the message box (F13), a tapped message keeping its buttons up (F11), and the message box riding the keyboard (W4).

Related records

Ledger §333 (held; Ask 0 ruled), §332 W1 (New room over the phone bar; untouched), §311 (chat posting "left no trace": this walk posted on every surface). TODO: the plain × for chat's panels, the Install banner over chat's confirm windows, F39 (Chat's paywall tab on the free phone bar).

Formatting check · the design review, 2026-10-18

What the design review changed in these drawings

Checked against the written rules and the coaches portal as the benchmark. All fourteen are applied above. They are proposals until you rule the drawings; none was written into the design log.

  1. Home's Chat count is red (the consumer tab badge), as today; the admin and portal bars keep their olive counts.
  2. Muted text uses the warm theme's muted ink (times, receipts, the box's hint), which clears the 4.5:1 contrast floor; the red and amber are the warm theme's own.
  3. The free portal at a computer has no banner: its rail names the team with the game-day chip and event, as it does today (drawing 13).
  4. Copy link and Mute (72 h) are olive worded actions, 44 px on a phone and 38 px at a desk; the Email action that Manage room has today is kept (drawings 9 and 10).
  5. One message timeline across all drawings: each list's last message and time match the room beside it.
  6. No separate Staff tag: a staff room says so in its name, once, on every door; home keeps its own list column width.
  7. Unchanged chrome is drawn whole: the active tab's pill and dot, the More count, the side menu's Chat count, the bell's count, Public site, the portal's Next line, the olive Workspaces pill.
  8. Room details keep everything Manage room has: each member's team and last seen, Mute (72 h), all three members at a desk.
  9. Home's list shows every room it shows today, including the No Metrics team's staff room.
  10. The read receipt carries its double tick everywhere.
  11. Each room starts with its Yesterday line, and the New messages line sits only above messages from others.
  12. Each reaction in the menu is a 44 px target; a moderator's menu has Remove instead of Report (the standard's wording now says so).
  13. The hover ⌄ is a rounded square, not a circle (the coaches portal bans circle buttons, and the panel is shared).
  14. "2 not joined" is the amber waiting pill in the room's line, never words after a name.

Chat Consistency — one messaging app, everywhere chat exists

⏸ SHELVED 2026-10-18: the owner ruled CHAT_EVALUATION.md E1 (chat pauses). Nothing here is built. The standard W1–W7 and the findings stay as the reference for the future Messages screens (E2, E4); the ladder and the 13 drawing asks are not pursued.

Walked 2026-10-18 (four surfaces, 390 · 960 · 1280 wide, in a headless browser on the dev server). Asks 0 and 1 ruled 2026-10-18. The end state is drawn on the hub's Drawings tab, each changed part tagged with the stage that delivers it. Nothing here is built. The build prompt is written once the owner rules the drawings.

Hub (walk, standard, ladder, drawings, asks): https://claude.ai/artifact/HsTsarRgc4fxjtLZ8Z3DVQ. Brief: CHAT_CONSISTENCY_PM_BRIEF.md. Kickoff: CHAT_CONSISTENCY_REVIEW_PROMPT.md. Umbrella: PROGRAM_COACH_CHAT.md.

1 · The ask, and the standard as ruled

Owner, 2026-10-18, on the organizer's Chat on a phone: "I still don't like it, not sure why we deviated away but the chat is supposed to mimic the whatsapp chat functionality everywhere that it exists (home, coaches portal, tournament)… review all of these screens for functional consistency and make sure that they all behave as expected."

Ask 0 (ruled 2026-10-18): undo §333's phone layout, keep two. The hidden room header, the framed card and search in the pill row were undone in the working tree the same day. The message box's hint that names who a message reaches ("Write to all coaches…", "Write to U13 Boys…") and the disabled Send button's standard fade stay. §332's fix on the same screen (New room closes the rooms list and covers the phone bar) was left alone.

Ask 1 (ruled 2026-10-18): the standard, adopted with the session's amendments. Every surface is measured against it.

  • W1 · A phone opens on the list. The chats you can open, newest activity first, an unread count per row. A lone room may open straight into its conversation.
  • W2 · Tap a row and the conversation fills the screen. No page title band, no picker, no banner above it. The app's bottom bar hides inside an open conversation (ruled 2026-10-18); back returns to the list, where it is.
  • W3 · The conversation's header is the only chrome. Back on the left, the room's name with one line under it (who it reaches), its tools on the right (search). Back is always there on a phone and always goes to the list, even when a lone room opened by itself. Tapping the room's name opens its details: who is in it, Mute, and Manage for whoever moderates.
  • W4 · The message box sits on the bottom edge and rides above the keyboard; its hint says who the message reaches.
  • W5 · A computer is the split: the list on the left, the conversation on the right, the full width beside the portal's own side menu, no back.
  • W6 · One behaviour per gesture, everywhere. Press and hold a message opens the same menu on every surface (what is in it varies by role, never where it lives). On a computer, right-click opens that same menu. Reply, react, mention, search, read receipts, the unread line and pins work the same everywhere.
  • W7 · One breakpoint for list ↔ split on every surface. The walk's 960 check sets the number (§3, station 3).

Settled, not reopened: staff rooms are per team and nobody inherits staff-room history (CH-5); no chat email, push and the Chat tab's count only; family chat was cut; the free plan's Chat stays behind the Tournament Plus wall (A60); a lone room opens by itself on home.

2 · How the walk was run

  • Fixture (dev only): a test event, UAT Chat Review Cup, on the Plus test club, with two rooms (All coaches and U13 Boys). In them: the organizer (the Plus club's owner, shown as Ellen Park), the Premium coach (shown as Chris Hadley, UAT Test Team, who also has three staff rooms) and the free coach (shown as Frankie Okafor, UAT Free Team). Two more teams have no coach signed up ("2 not joined"). The staff room has an assistant (Nadia Ferreira). Seeded by a throwaway probe; the rows stay in dev so the owner can walk the same rooms.
  • Widths: 390 × 844 (phone), 960 × 800 (inside the gap where the breakpoints disagree) and 1280 × 800.
  • Behaviour: on every surface the walk posted, replied, reacted, mentioned, searched and deleted, and posted from another account while each list was open, then into a room the person was not looking at.
  • What a headless browser cannot show (marked "check on a real phone" below): the real keyboard, an iPhone's zoom on a small field, and how a phone holds a hover after a tap.
  • The hub (CHAT_CONSISTENCY_HUB.html, this folder) is built from .probe/chat-review/hub.src.html by .probe/chat-review/hub-build.mjs, which inlines the captures and renders this plan and the brief into it. .probe/ is gitignored scratch: if it is gone, edit the built hub directly.

Behaviour that matched everywhere: posting, replying (the quote shows), @mentions (the picker and the highlight), search ("parking" found 2 on every surface) and read receipts.

4 · Findings

F01 — A push always opens the home chat

Today: every chat push links to /chat?room=… (lib/chat-service.ts:1575, :1588), for coaches and organizers alike. Neither portal nor the organizer's page reads a room from its address. The walk opened the push link as the organizer: it landed in home chat. Effect: an organizer who taps a push lands where they cannot moderate (F02); a coach working in the portal is taken out of it. Proposal: keep the landing (Ask C4) and make home complete (C3); no notification change. Stage: C.

F02 — What you can do depends on the door you came through

Today: the organizer is a moderator member of every room, so the same rooms show in their home chat, where a tap gives only react and reply: no pin, remove, poll or Manage (app/(consumer)/chat/ChatConversation.tsx:78-85). A staff room's head coach pins and removes in the portal, not at home. Report and Mute exist only at home; the portals pass no press-and-hold. Proposal: what you can do follows who you are in the room, on every door (R2). The server already allows it; the hosts do not pass it. Stage: C.

F03 — The organizer has no list

Today: the page always opens All coaches (app/[orgSlug]/admin/tournaments/chat/page.tsx:110-114). The other rooms sit behind the olive pill on a phone and in a docked column at a desk; neither shows an unread count, the last message or a time (page.tsx:367-385, components/chat/ChatRoomsPanel.tsx:113-146). Every other surface has all three. Proposal: the organizer's phone opens on a list; the desk column is the same list. Stage: A.

F04 — Three designs for one list, two names for one room

Today: home lists flat rows under event and team headings (time, sender prefix, olive count, a muted bell). The portals list bordered cards (Staff and Closed tags, "Your coaching staff", a lime count, no time, no muted bell). The All coaches room is "All coaches" at home and "UAT Chat Review Cup — Coaches" in the portals. The organizer's rooms list says "members"; its pill and column say "coaches". Home repeats a division room's name as its line ("U13 Boys", "U13 Boys"). Code note: the portal's "this team first" test looks for /coaches/teams/, so it never matches a free address (components/chat/CoachChatView.tsx:108); harmless today, since free coaches have no staff rooms. Proposal: one row recipe and one name (R3). Stage: A.

F05 — No list updates while you look at it

Today: with each list open, a message arrived in All coaches. On home, paid and free the row's last message, its count and its place stayed as they were; only the Chat tab's badge counted up. The portals' list never fetches again, not even after Back (CoachChatView.tsx:110-131); home fetches again on Back only. Proposal: a new message moves its row to the top and counts it (R3). Stage: A.

F06 — The organizer's open room is boxed in

Today (phone): the event band, the Chat title band and the pill row take 190 px above the room. The conversation gets 464 px between its header and the message box, against 557 (free), 602 (home) and 646 (paid). There is no back. Proposal: the room fills the screen (R4). Stage: B.

F07 — The bottom bar stays in an open room, and hides while typing on two surfaces only

Today: the 72 px bar stays under every open room. While the message box has focus, home and the free portal hide it; the paid portal and the organizer do not. Proposal: hidden in an open room (W2, ruled). Stage: B.

F08 — The free portal: opening a room with unread messages scrolls the page under the team banner

Today (2 of 2 opens): the page scrolls 89 px, so the room's header (back, name, search) sits under the team banner, and a 90 px blank band opens between the message box and the bottom bar. The jump to the "New messages" line scrolls every scrollable container, the page's included (components/chat/ChatPanel.tsx:509); a comment at :360 warns of exactly this for another scroll. It does not show on home or the paid portal, whose pages cannot scroll there. Proposal: scroll the message list only. A defect: it can ship ahead of the rest. Stage: B.

F09 — A banner over an open room on two surfaces

Today: the paid portal hides the team banner at 640 and under but shows it from 641 to 900; the free portal keeps it (89 px). Proposal: nothing above an open room on a phone (W2). Stage: B.

F10 — Four header recipes

Today: home: ‹ (40 px), name, search, an event chip (28 px, no accessible name on a phone); the organizer at home also gets "Event admin" (28 px, no accessible name). Portals: ‹ (44 px) only with two or more rooms, the stored name, search, "?" (32 px); the "Rooms" word beside ‹ is hidden at every width it shows. Organizer: no back; the name over "Every coach with a team in this tournament" in code type; search; Manage room sits on the page title above. Proposal: one header (R4). Stage: B.

F11 — A message's buttons float over the message above it

Today: tapping a message shows react and reply (plus delete for your own, pin and remove for a moderator) in a cluster above the bubble, covering the words of the message above. The same cluster shows on hover, and that hover rule is not limited to devices that can hover (components/chat/ChatPanel.module.css:472-497), so on a phone a message can keep its buttons up after another is tapped (seen in the walk; check on a real phone). Proposal: a tap does nothing; press and hold opens one menu (R5). Stage: C.

F12 — Press and hold means three different things

Today: at home, holding a message (or right-clicking it) opens Report to organizers · Mute this room · Cancel, with no reply, react or delete. On the organizer's page and both portals, holding does nothing and right-click opens the browser's own menu. Mute is a room setting, kept in a menu about one message. Proposal: one menu (R5); Mute moves to room details (R6). Stage: C.

F13 — The message box's text is 14 px

Today: an iPhone zooms the page when a field under 16 px is tapped, and the app does not prevent it (app/layout.tsx:50-59; the box at ChatPanel.module.css:792). Every surface. Check on a real iPhone. Proposal: 16 px. Stage: B.

F14 — The organizer gets no "New messages" line

Today: the page passes no unread count to the conversation (ChatPanel.tsx:496-500), so an organizer coming back to a busy room has no marker for where they left off. Proposal: the same line as every other surface. Stage: A.

F15 — The reply quote is a heavy box

Today: every reply carries a grey box with a 2 px near-black border, on every surface. WhatsApp's quote is a tinted strip with a coloured edge and the sender's name. Proposal: the tinted strip. Stage: C.

F16 — Room tools live in three places

Today: the organizer's Manage room is a button on the page title; home's Mute is inside a message's hold; the portals have no Mute, no Report and no members list. Proposal: tap the room's name to open its details (W3, R6). Stage: C.

F17 — Enter sends on a phone

Today: the return key sends (ChatPanel.tsx:1272). In WhatsApp the return key adds a line on a phone and the Send button sends. Proposal: Ask B3. Stage: B.

F18 — Two loose ends

Today: a poll's push carries no link and opens the home page (chat-service.ts:2092-2100, public/sw.js:288). A signed-out coach opening the paid portal's Chat is sent to the portal's front page after signing in, not back to Chat (app/[orgSlug]/coaches/layout.tsx:79). Proposal: both open the room. Stage: D.

F19 — Two breakpoints

Today: 900 on the organizer's page, 1024 on home and the portals. At 960 the organizer's conversation is 376 px wide; the others show one pane. Proposal: 1024 everywhere (W7). Stage: D.

F20 — The portal's list column is too narrow at a desk

Today: at 1280 the paid portal's list column is 264 px, and room names wrap to two lines inside their cards. Proposal: the list column matches home's (300 to 400 px) once its rows are the shared row. Stage: D.

5 · Standing back: the rules that cut across the stations

  • R1 · One chat, four doors. The same three parts on every door: the list, the open room, and the room's details. A door decides which rooms are listed and the colours around them, nothing else.
  • R2 · What you can do follows who you are in the room. A moderator moderates on every door; a staff room's head coach pins on every door; everyone can reply, react, delete their own and mute on every door, and everyone who does not moderate can report.
  • R3 · One list row, and a live list. Avatar, the room's one name, time, the last message with its sender, the unread count; Staff and Closed tags; a muted bell. A new message moves its row to the top and counts it.
  • R4 · One open room on a phone. It fills the screen. Header: ‹ · avatar · name over one line (who it reaches) · search. Nothing above it and no bottom bar; the message box on the bottom edge, 16 px, a hint naming who it reaches.
  • R5 · One message menu. Press and hold (phone), right-click or the hover ⌄ (computer) opens a row of reactions, then Reply · Copy · Pin (moderators) · Delete (your own) or Remove (moderators) · Report (someone else's, for anyone who does not moderate; a moderator removes instead). A tap does nothing.
  • R6 · One room-details screen. Tap the room's name: who is in it, Mute notifications, and for a moderator the coaches not yet joined (copy their sign-up link), reports to review, Rename, Close and Delete. The organizer's Manage room becomes this screen.
  • R7 · One breakpoint, 1024. Below it, list ↔ room; at 1024 and over, the split, full width beside the side menu.

6 · The ladder

Each stage changes one part of the app on all four doors at once, so no stage leaves the surfaces more different than it found them. (The kickoff's draft built the organizer's phone first; built alone, that would have added a fourth list design before the shared row existed.)

7 · The end state, screen by screen

Drawn at true size on the hub's Drawings tab: before (a capture from the walk) beside after (drawn), every changed part tagged A, B, C or D with a note behind it.

  • Organizer, phone: the list (new), then the open room filling the screen.
  • Home, phone: the list (one name; live), the open room (bar hidden, the event link moved to details).
  • Coaches portal (paid and free), phone: the list as rows, not cards; the open room with nothing above it.
  • Every door: the message menu (press and hold) and room details (tap the name), each with the organizer's extra rows marked.
  • Computer: the organizer's split with details as a right-hand panel; home; the paid portal; the free portal.
  • Formatting check (the design review, 2026-10-18): fourteen fixes applied to the drawings before the hand-off, listed at the foot of the hub's Drawings tab. They are proposals until the drawings are ruled; none went into the design log.

8 · Asks for the owner (each beside the drawing that answers it)

  • A1 · The organizer's list keeps the event band (which event, and the switcher) and a "Chat" title row holding ＋ New room and "?". Recommended. What rides on it: the admin's event context stays one tap from the switcher.
  • A2 · "Not joined" lives in the room's line and its details, not on the list row ("3 members · 2 not joined", the count as the amber waiting pill). Recommended. Two counts on one row compete; the unread count is the one a row exists for.
  • A3 · One name: "All coaches", with the event as its heading at home and its line in the portals. Recommended.
  • A4 · Each door keeps its grouping (home by event and team; the portal: this team, its events, then your other teams; the organizer: this event's rooms) with one row recipe. Recommended.
  • B1 · "?" moves from the room's header to the list's title row. Recommended. The header keeps its tools to search.
  • B2 · The event chip and "Event admin" leave the header for room details ("Open the event", "Manage in event admin"). Recommended.
  • B3 · On a phone the return key adds a line; Send sends. At a computer Enter still sends. Recommended.
  • C1 · The menu holds: reactions, Reply, Copy, Pin (moderators), Delete (your own) or Remove (moderators), Report (someone else's, for anyone who does not moderate). Recommended. Copy is new.
  • C2 · A tap on a message does nothing; the floating buttons go. Recommended. Swipe to reply is "Not yet".
  • C3 · What you can do follows your role on every door (R2). Recommended. No permission change; the server already allows it.
  • C4 · A push still opens the home chat. Recommended. With C3 nothing is missing there, and the seam (sign in, then the room) already works.
  • D1 · 1024 everywhere. Recommended. Measured: at 960 the organizer's conversation is 376 px.
  • D2 · At a computer, room details open as a panel to the right of the conversation, as WhatsApp's desktop does, not a separate page. Recommended.

Not yet: searching older messages (search reads the loaded messages today, the same on every surface); swipe to reply; a typing indicator; editing a message.

9 · What this plan does not change, and the risks

  • No data, permission or notification change. C3 uses permissions the server already enforces; C4 keeps every push's link. The two link fixes in D are the only notification-adjacent change, and both make an existing link open the room it names.
  • The shared conversation panel changes once per stage for four surfaces. Each stage is walked on all four.
  • Demo sandboxes: the build fails if a tour anchor disappears; check the coach and tournament tours' chat stops at build time (the organizer's chat changes shape in A).
  • Help content: the chat guides on every door change (/docs after each stage).
  • Real-phone checks owed: the iPhone zoom (F13), the sticky hover (F11), the keyboard riding the message box (W4).

Chat Consistency — PM brief

Walked and drawn 2026-10-18; shelved the same day when the owner ruled the evaluation below (E1–E6 as recommended: chat pauses). Plan: CHAT_CONSISTENCY_PLAN.md.

The bigger question first (evaluation, 2026-10-18)

The owner asked whether chat should stay at all, and ruled the evaluation's answer the same day (CHAT_EVALUATION.md, the hub's first tab): chat pauses now, because it is staff-only, it reaches people only through phone notifications (an iPhone needs the app installed; Android delivery is unconfirmed; nothing is emailed), and email tools already reach the same people. No paying customer uses it and no plan card sells it, so pausing is cheap and reversible. Messaging would return later as announcements that reach everyone, with replies, for families in the Club tier, on the safeguarding rules Canadian sport requires. If the owner rules to keep chat instead, the consistency work below is the plan, plus a delivery fix.

What changes for people

Chat exists in four places: the home app, the paid coaches portal, the free coaches portal, and the tournament organizer's admin. Today they are four slightly different apps. After this work they are one, and it behaves like the messaging app everyone already knows.

  • Every door opens on a list of chats: one row per room with its name, the last message, the time and an unread count, and the list updates as messages arrive. The organizer gets a list for the first time; today their phone drops them straight into one room.
  • Opening a chat fills the phone screen: back on the left, the room's name and who it reaches, search, and the message box on the bottom edge. The app's bottom bar steps away while you are in a conversation and comes back with the list.
  • Press and hold a message, anywhere, for the same menu: react, reply, copy, and (for whoever moderates) pin or remove; report someone else's message. On a computer, right-click does the same.
  • Tap a room's name for its details: who is in it, mute, and for the organizer everything "Manage room" does today.
  • What you can do follows who you are, not where you opened it. An organizer who taps a chat notification can moderate right there; a coach can report and mute from the coaches portal too.

Why it matters

The owner's standard for chat has been "like WhatsApp" since June, but each surface drifted on its own. The walk found an organizer's phone giving the conversation less room than any other surface (464 px of messages against 602 at home), three different list designs, one room called by two names, lists that never update while open, three meanings for press and hold, and a free-portal defect that hides the room's back button behind the team banner whenever a room has unread messages.

Customer impact

  • Organizers (Tournament Plus and up) run game-day communication from a phone. They get a real inbox, more room to read, and moderation wherever a notification lands them.
  • Coaches on both portals get the same chat as the home app, including report and mute, and a list that tells the truth about what is unread.
  • Free coaches stop losing the room's header and back button on every unread room (the defect can ship first).

Priority

High within the chat program: chat is a Tournament Plus selling point and the organizer's phone screen is what the owner flagged. The work is front-end only: no data, permission or notification change.

Success criteria

  • The owner walks all four doors on a phone and a computer and finds the same list, the same open room, the same menu and the same details screen.
  • An organizer can open a push, read, and moderate without leaving the room.
  • A new message moves its room to the top of an open list and counts it, on every door.
  • No room header hides behind a banner, and an iPhone does not zoom when the message box is tapped.

Stages

A · one list → B · one open room → C · one message menu and room details → D · one computer split and the loose ends. Each stage changes all four doors at once.
